references.text: This section in Leviticus provides a detailed list of unclean birds that the Israelites were not to eat, which complements and expands on the principle of clean birds mentioned in Deuteronomy 14:11.
The entire chapter on clean and unclean animals in Leviticus provides the foundational framework for the food laws that Deuteronomy 14:11 builds upon.
The verses that follow immediately provide the list of unclean birds that are not to be eaten, in contrast to the clean birds mentioned in verse 11.
Peter's vision regarding clean and unclean animals shows how the distinctions from Deuteronomy 14:11 were fulfilled and set aside in the new covenant.
